messages:
kat: Quick report: generator sample in Go hit a hang when token refresh occurs mid-stream. iter.Next() sometimes blocks after ctx cancellation; leak detector showed goroutines.

rui: Thanks. which sdk version and example? can you paste the minimal loop?

kat: go-sdk v0.13.1, example loop: `ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Second); defer cancel(); iter, _ := client.Generator(ctx, p); for iter.Next() { process(iter.Value()) } if err := iter.Err(); err != nil { log.Println(err) }`

jena: Sample omitted `defer iter.Close()`? that's an important ownership detail.

kat: yeah original sample didn't call Close and assumed Next reacts to ctx cancel. adding `defer iter.Close()` fixed my repro locally.

eng-runtime-bot: CI alert: nightly stream-leak-check found 3 leaked goroutines in generator sample.

rui: Proposal: (1) short-term: update sample + README to show `defer iter.Close()` and add a test asserting Next returns soon after Close. (2) mid-term: make Close idempotent and ensure internal reader selects on both ctx.Done() and closeCh to unblock Next immediately. (3) long-term: consider `NextWithContext(ctx)` or `GeneratorWithCancel`.

jena: Also document the errors: if Close caused stop return ErrIteratorClosed; if user ctx canceled return context.Canceled. add errors.Is documentation so callers can detect both.

kat: I'll open a small sample/docs PR (low risk). rui/jena please own the SDK change making Close safe and add a fast-unblock test simulating token rotation.

ci-bot: Reminder: run `make sample-test` and `go test ./... -race` locally. CI will run stream-leak-checker.

rui: thanks — sounds actionable. I'll add a TODO design ticket for NextWithContext but defer API changes until we've hardened Close semantics.

kat: PR up shortly, linking repro. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
